items.value: I figured that this is fairly simple, as I got some working code for Saturn, that was never once used 😓...

The Rev Blinkin is technically just a really fancy Spark Motor that uses PWM that calls its Constants for the PWM Port. I'm mainly pulling from my example code for the Blinkin, so after importing Spark to control the LED stuff, we then use a pattern, which I don't have a video of particular patterns, but I've got this sheet to help out.

The left most one that isn't 56-88, that's a pulse width, then to the right of that is a Spark Motor Value (Again, in code it's a really fancy Spark Motor), then the pattern type, where typically there's a fixed palette pattern like Rainbow, or Confetti, or there are Color 1/2 Patterns that I think use colors defined in setup mode, then the pattern name, then the normal operation adjustments, with first one being pattern density typically, or pattern width, or dimming, then typically speed, and lastly is just brightness, though in setup mode, adj 1 is for color 1, adj 2 is for color 2, and brightness gets replaced with length, so your LEDs can be a certain length.
Ok, this has gotten a little large, I'll share some code examples later. If you want an example of Blinkin Code from Saturn

Ok, so first, we want to go to the Constants Class. We want to make a static class called BlinkinConstants. The first thing we'll add to the new class is a static final integer meant to indicate the PWM Port, I'm not sure what the PWM port setup will look like on the SystemCore, but on the RoboRIO, there's 10 ports labeled from 0-9. Then though it might be much. We want to add every possible combo into an enum, which is essentially a fixed list. You really only need to set values from the table to the values listed there, which is a double, you'll then make a double variable and a constructor for an enum, you could also add a String variable to have human readable text, but that's more work, essentially an enum could be described as a mini class.
After you set up the Constants class, it should look something akin to this:

Ok, so before I share the second part of the constants, yes the example code was from the 2026 Robot and I had set up stuff to allow people to change the constants for either the Goonettes Invitational, or a standard one, but the Blinkin was never used on the robot.
With that, we've now set up our constants to now have all possible values for the REV Blinkin. In the next post, I will share my setup of the Blinkin subsystem and share that with you.
Now that we've set up the Constants for the Rev Blinkin. It's now time to set up the real Blinkin Subsystem. This does assume we're using Commands V2.

Now, the Rev Blinkin is essentially a really fancy Spark Motor, so after making the subsystem for the Blinkin, we make a new variable of type Spark (wpilibj.motorcontrol.Spark), passing in the PWM port from our Constants. We then make a double, and then in my case, I added a boolean called isFiring to change the lighting when we are firing.

I believe another one I used is a SendableChooser of the enum we made in the constants to allow for a selectable option for custom colors during drive testing, so the constructor I made just sets up the Blinkin LED Pattern table, which pretty much just sets a default option, runs a for loop for all values in the enum and adds them aside from the first one we added, then putting that all into an LED Pattern data table.

Next up is the periodic, the first lines I put were related to getting the current command or if we were idle. Then I checked if Teleop is enabled through DriverStation.isTeleopEnabled. where I then get the match time, get game specific data, and then run an if statement checking if it's empty, time is greater than 130 seconds or time is less than or equal to 30, I use a custom method called easyChoice, which is genuinely just an if statement to set the colors for the alliance to either a set of patterns I used for default matches or the Goonettes Invitational, and an option for setting a custom color.

Afterwards, I then added a variable named myAlliance, which is of type Alliance (Though for some reason I used the auto variable type, which means it reads as var myAlliance), that gets the alliance or it's the red alliance. Then I make a boolean called weAreInactiveFirst that checks the game data and then uses a ternary operator (A shorthand if-else statement) to check if we are first the red alliance, then if that's the case, the method checks if the value starts with Blue, otherwise the method checks for Red, well, the first letter as that's the game data that gets transferred to the robot, of course, this ternary operator is to check if we're looking for if the game data transmits B whilst we're on the red alliance, or R when on the blue alliance.

Afterwards the periodic function checks the time and then sets the shift. Then in the shifts, if we're inactive first, and in shifts 1 or 3, then it runs the inactive lighting, otherwise it goes into phase mode, and if we're in auton, then it just runs the inactive lighting.
I'll share more about the methods later.
